title: Ashwin Says Only Bumrah Is Locked In as India's 2027 World Cup Pace Race Tightens
excerpt: R Ashwin said Jasprit Bumrah is the only fast bowler certain of a 2027 ODI World Cup place, and that Mohammed Siraj, for all his experience, is not a lock given how little ODI cricket India have given him. Prasidh Krishna, Arshdeep Singh and Anshul Kamboj are all in the race, he said.
body:
• R Ashwin said Jasprit Bumrah is the only fast bowler completely locked into India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
  • On Mohammed Siraj, Ashwin said he hopes the experienced pacer makes it but is not sure he is locked in, given how sparingly India have used him in ODIs; Siraj has played just four ODIs in 2026, according to Sportskeeda's account.
  • Between the tall pacers Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar, Ashwin put Prasidh slightly ahead; he also credited Arshdeep Singh's performances and said Anshul Kamboj should not be counted out.
  • In his own five-man pace pick for the squad, Ashwin named Bumrah, Prasidh, Siraj, Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep.

Ravichandran Ashwin has said that only one Indian fast bowler, Jasprit Bumrah, is certain of a place in India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, and that Mohammed Siraj's spot is not guaranteed despite his experience. Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin assessed the crowded field of pace contenders for the tournament, which is scheduled in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2 to November 21, 2027, Circle of Cricket reported.

"The race will be very close. Bumrah is locked in. But the way we have used Siraj, I am not sure if he is locked in. I hope he is, because he has the experience. Between Prasidh and Gurnoor, I feel Prasidh is slightly ahead. Arshdeep has also done well. Don't count out Anshul. I think they will have to pick and choose. All of them are in the race for the World Cup squad."

— R Ashwin, on his YouTube channel, via Circle of Cricket

The Case on Siraj

Ashwin's doubt is about usage, not ability. Siraj has played just four ODIs so far in 2026 and has not been used much by India in the format, Sportskeeda noted in its account of the same comments. A bowler cannot be a World Cup lock, the argument runs, if the team itself keeps leaving him out of the format the World Cup is played in. Ashwin said he would like to see Siraj play more in the coming months and get back into rhythm.

The Rest of the Race

Comparing the two tall pacers, Ashwin gave Prasidh Krishna a slight edge over Gurnoor Brar, while noting Prasidh would need to be fit and firing to make the squad. Arshdeep Singh, India's leading wicket-taker in T20Is, has also done well, he said, and emerging pacer Anshul Kamboj should not be ruled out. On Auqib Nabi, Ashwin was cooler, saying his pace is still low and questioning whether he will be in World Cup contention. In the five-man pace attack Ashwin himself picked for the squad, he named Bumrah, Prasidh, Siraj, all-rounder Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep, a list that includes Siraj even as he questions the selectors' commitment to him.

What It Means

India are using their ODI series in the run-up to 2027 to trial pace options and combinations, and Ashwin's comments are a senior player's reading of that process: one certainty, and every other place earned in the months ahead. The selectors' handling of Siraj, whether he gets a sustained ODI run or keeps being rotated out, will be the clearest signal of whether Ashwin's doubt was well placed.
